clue.text: Form is stocked with 100 great books

parts.note: a form is a school class

indicators.note: a word stocked with something holds it inside, so the small word takes a letter into its middle

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A school form whose shelves are well supplied with a hundred great books.
explanation.definitionFit: The classics are the great works of literature, especially those of Greece and Rome.

clue.text: Capturer of pictures of the first person embraced by woman

indicators.note: the first person is hugged by the woman, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: Cara is a woman's name
me is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A camera taking pictures of the narrator being hugged by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is the device that records photographs, so it captures images.

clue.text: Voice — it returns in cave eerily

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the mixed-up letters
eerily suggests something strange, so the letters of the word cave are mixed up
returns means the word it goes back to front

explanation.surface: A voice echoing back eerily inside a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voice' suggests speech, but it is the grammar term for a verb form; 'eerily' gives ACVE, which holds the turned pair.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the active voice is one of the two voices of a verb, the other being passive.

clue.text: Religious meal in which prophet entertains 500

indicators.note: the prophet entertains, or hosts, the number, so it goes inside his word

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A prophet hosting five hundred guests at a sacred dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' puts D inside SEER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seder is the ritual Jewish feast held on the first night or nights of Passover.

clue.text: Grumbling, being bothered about parking

indicators.note: about means around, so the caring word goes around the letter

parts.note: caring means being concerned or bothered
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone complaining because they are fretting over parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CARING round P.
explanation.definitionFit: Carping means constantly finding fault and complaining, which is grumbling.

clue.text: Mount desert animal to cross river

indicators.note: the animal is made to cross the river, read as letters set across it, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: the camel is the beast of the desert

explanation.surface: Climb onto a camel to ford a river in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb about getting on the camel; it is a noun, the definition. 'to cross' puts R inside CAMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Carmel is a mountain ridge in Israel, near Haifa, named in the Bible.

clue.text: Notice something being said in worship

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
an oration is a speech

explanation.surface: Spotting something spoken during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep reverence or love, especially of God, which is worship.

clue.text: Arrives before one to get into game, rescheduled match

indicators.note: the joined letters get into the reworked game word, so they sit inside it
rescheduled means rearranged, so the letters of game are shuffled
the arrival letters go before the single letter

parts.note: arr. is the abbreviation for arrives on timetables
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rearranged fixture, with a late arrival joining the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a sporting fixture; it is a union of two people. 'rescheduled' turns GAME into MAGE; 'to get into' puts ARRI inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a match in the sense of a union of a couple.

clue.text: Old-style solicitor with some flaw, a gentleman

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned lawyer who is something of a flawed gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Law agent is a dated term, chiefly Scottish, for a solicitor who acts for clients.

clue.text: From what we hear, actor Smith loves men fighting

indicators.note: this phrase says the following words are to be heard, not read, so their sound gives the entry

parts.note: Matt Smith is the actor, best known as Doctor Who, and 'Matt adores' means he loves

explanation.surface: A gossipy remark that the actor Smith fancies men who fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'Matt adores' gives the bullfighters.
explanation.definitionFit: Matadors are the bullfighters who kill the bull, so they are men engaged in combat.

clue.text: English author to obtain from library?

definitions.meaning: George ... was a 19th-century English writer of travel books such as Lavengro
taking a book out on loan; the question mark flags that a library lends

explanation.surface: Taking out a book by an English writer from the lending library.
explanation.definitionFit: George Borrow is the English author; to take a book on loan is the everyday verb sense.

clue.text: Swimmer beginning to worry with tide going out

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word is its first letter

parts.note: the ebb is the outgoing tide

explanation.surface: A swimmer starting to fret as the tide recedes.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Matthew Webb was the first person to swim the English Channel, in 1875.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Webb is a famous swimmer, the first to cross the Channel unaided.

clue.text: Bank interest rates initially revised after crash

indicators.note: after a crash things lie in a jumble, so the gathered letters are rearranged
initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A bank revising its interest rates in the wake of a financial crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' reads as the money lender; it is a river's edge. 'initially' gives IR, which joins REVISED; 'after crash' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A riverside is the land along a river's edge, which is what a river bank is.

clue.text: A side is amazing

parts.note: a wing is a side of a building, or of a football team

explanation.surface: A remark that one team or faction is wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Awing is an adjective meaning inspiring wonder or awe, close to astonishing or overwhelming.

clue.text: Drop off as junior public schoolboy tackling Latin

indicators.note: the schoolboy takes on, or grips, the language, so the abbreviation sits inside his word

parts.note: at British public (private) schools a fag was a junior boy who ran errands for a senior

explanation.surface: A young boarding-school pupil nodding off while tackling his Latin homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackling' puts L inside FAG. A fag in British boarding schools was a younger boy who served an older one.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire and weaken, as energy or interest drops off.

clue.text: Vital cure could be moneymaking

indicators.note: could be means the letters might be arranged in another order

explanation.surface: An essential remedy might turn a tidy profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative means profitable, producing plenty of wealth.

clue.text: Introduce intellectual, having poured out a drink

indicators.note: pouring out removes something, so the A is taken out of the word for the clever person

parts.note: a brain is a clever person, an intellectual
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Introducing a clever guest who has just poured themselves a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having poured out' takes A from BRAIN, leaving BRIN, followed by GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something in is to introduce it, as with a new law or system.

clue.text: One to flatter in the most sincere way?

definitions.text: One to flatter in the most sincere way?

parts.words: One to flatter in the most sincere way?
parts.note: plays on the saying that copying someone is the sincerest form of flattery

explanation.surface: Someone who compliments others with complete honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says copying is the sincerest form of flattery, so the copier flatters most sincerely.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier or mimic, by the proverb, pays the sincerest compliment of all.

clue.text: What's shown by one with endless lolling around?

definitions.text: What's shown by one with endless lolling around?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: lolling around suggests sprawling loosely, so the letters of endless are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking what quality a person forever lounging about displays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lolling around' rearranges ENDLESS; 'with' joins it to I. The whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Laziness or inactivity is what endless lounging displays.

clue.text: Examination — one of those coming down here is confused!

indicators.note: something confused is mixed up, so the letters of that down entry are rearranged

parts.words: one of those coming down here
parts.note: the clue points to a down entry in this very grid, 21-down, whose solution is the verb meaning to lecture

explanation.surface: A doctor's examination where a patient being stretchered down is muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'one of those coming down' is a down answer in this grid, 21-down, the speechifying verb, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical examination by a doctor, for a job or insurance.

clue.text: Go over items presented systematically

definitions.meaning: a ship that tilts or leans to one side goes over
a series of things set out in order, such as names

explanation.surface: Reviewing a set of things laid out in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that leans lists; an ordered set of items written down is also this.

clue.text: Lady's title provided by steward on arrival

indicators.note: the letters are supplied by the words that follow, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A steward greets a lady with her proper title as she arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Doña is the Spanish honorific placed before a lady's name, matching Don for men.

clue.text: Lecture using new media to entertain 150

indicators.note: the rearranged word entertains, or takes in, the number, so it sits inside
new suggests a fresh form, so the letters of media are rearranged

parts.note: CL is the Roman numeral for 150

explanation.surface: A talk using fresh media to keep an audience of 150 amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lecture' is a verb here, meaning to harangue; 'new' gives DEAIM, which takes the Roman numeral inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak rhetorically or harangue, as if giving a lecture.

clue.text: Bandleader in factory meeting HM

indicators.note: the factory word meets the royal one, joining side by side

parts.note: a mill is a factory
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is Her Majesty the Queen

explanation.surface: A band leader at a factory being introduced to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Glenn Miller was the American bandleader of the swing era.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenn Miller led one of the most famous big bands of the 1940s.

clue.text: Not informed, as very many may be

definitions.meaning: too numerous to count, as in countless riches

explanation.surface: Kept in the dark, as large numbers of people often are.
explanation.definitionFit: Not having been told is the literal sense; numberless or countless is the idiomatic one.

clue.text: Greek letter that is half-obscured by an earlier one

indicators.note: half of the word is covered, leaving only its first two letters showing

parts.note: eta is a Greek letter coming before the one wanted in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek letter partly blocked from view by a letter coming before it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is half-obscured' leaves TH; the earlier Greek letter is ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet, written as a barred circle.

clue.text: Partisan as certain as could be

indicators.note: the letters could be arranged otherwise, signalling that they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A one-sided supporter being utterly sure of their view.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectarian describes narrow, bigoted loyalty to one faction, which is what partisan means.

clue.text: Any number in region where sport can be watched

indicators.note: in places the number inside the region word

parts.note: an area is a region
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A district holding any number of places to watch games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside AREA.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a stadium or venue with seating for spectators of events.

clue.text: Article by relative that may have been written at university

definitions.text: that may have been written at university

parts.note: the is the definite article
sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: A piece written by a family member, possibly while studying at college.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a long dissertation produced by a student for a degree.

clue.text: End of the line — not just for a French supremo

definitions.text: End of the line — not just for a French supremo

parts.words: End of the line — not just for a French supremo
parts.note: Napoleon met his final defeat at the 1815 battle in Belgium, now a byword for anyone's ultimate downfall; the London terminus of that name is also literally the end of a railway line

explanation.surface: Final defeat comes to many people, not only to a French emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon's last battle gave English the phrase 'meet one's Waterloo', meaning any decisive defeat; Waterloo is also a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A final, crushing defeat is the idiomatic sense, from Napoleon's battle, and that is the end of the line for anyone.

clue.text: After game the female had got her skates on?

indicators.note: the female's pieces come after the game in the answer

parts.note: RU is rugby union
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: After a match, a woman had put her ice skates on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got her skates on' is British slang for hurrying.
explanation.definitionFit: To get your skates on is an idiom for hurrying, so having done it means having hastened.

clue.text: Spoilt child being naughty gets exposed

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
aired means exposed to the air or made public

explanation.surface: A spoilt child misbehaving and having their antics made public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoilt' suggests the indulged child, but it means damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means damaged or weakened, the sense of spoilt as in ruined.
